# Evaluation report (generated by `python -m src.eval.run --report`; do not edit by hand)

LLM used for every system in this report: **deepseek** (results in `data\processed\eval\deepseek_hints`). Numbers from different LLMs are never mixed.

**Read this first.** The test set is small, part of it is written by Claude (synthetic, not checked by a customs expert), and the real part comes from public Pakistani rulings (mostly one Karachi classification committee) and leans to machinery, electronics and chemicals. Intervals are wide. Real and synthetic results are never averaged. Systems are compared on the same cases only.

## Citation correctness (full graph only; other systems give no citations)

Answers with citations: 1. Citations checked: 100% (3/3; 95% CI 44-100%) point at a real fact row (tariff line on the date with the same file and page, or a store row for that file and page). This checks the pointer, not the legal claim.


## Duty match (hand-computed bills)

Full graph: 100% (2/2; 95% CI 34-100%) bills equal the hand-computed total to the paisa.

## Baseline: Danial's TariffAI

TariffAI (MIT per its README; reference only, no code copied) ran from its own folder on the same cases. Differences from the original: Qdrant in local mode instead of Docker, and its single LLM call goes to the same DeepSeek flash model instead of Gemini (same prompt, same parsing). It classifies into the international 6-digit HS list, not Pakistan's 8-digit tariff, so it is scored at 4 and 6 digits only. Its 'ambiguous' flag (confidence below 0.7) is counted as asking/not sure.
